newsitem.title: UK: Olivetti London meeting gains muted favour.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti London meeting gains muted favour.

text.p: Troubled Italian technology and telecommunications group Olivetti SpA's management team gained a positive response from analysts at a meeting in London on Friday but the company still has a lot to do, they said.
"The chief executive and his team got a good reception but they have it all to do," said one person attending who asked not to be identified.

New chief executive Roberto Colaninno along with executives Luciano La Noce and Corrado Ariaudo fielded a range of questions from London-based analysts but sometimes struggled to provide detailed information, those at the meeting said.
"We need more detailed information, they did not seem to have it to hand," said one banking source.
"It is very much wait and see at the moment," he added.
Olivetti is presenting plans for recovery which include asset sales aimed at raising a total 1.2 trillion lire.
Colaninno told the meeting that talks over the sale of its personal computer business were under way and that the business must be sold by the end of the year.
"We heard what we anticipated," the bank source said.
